attempt: ONE. No retry, no second prompt variant, and no tuning after any eval output is seen. **The attempt is SPENT at the first GOLD-row reply generated** — not at pod create, not at a dev reply, and not at the dev gate, whose 200 rows are labelled comments outside both the sealed fourteen and the eval pack's sixty-four. A session that closes before any gold row is answered has NOT spent it and returns to the team lead, and every rung before rung 8 closes the session in exactly that state
authority: the operator's ruling of 2026-08-21 in the team-lead session, registered in docs/STATUS.md «Открытые решения» п. 3: re-register, and the STEP budget stays $1.50 all-in — r1's pods already bought $0.117783 of it, so r2's cap is $1.38. dev_gate.reachability: our_v2 ≤ 49, so the delta is unreachable whenever our_base > 39. That is a STOP, not a RED: the gate could not have been met by any v2 whatever, the attempt is NOT spent, and the table goes to the operator with the reading
dev_gate.rule: paired on the same 200 rows: our_v2 − our_base ≥ 10 (correct rows among the 49 категория_личное/молочный_бренд labels) AND agree_v2 − agree_base ≥ -5 (over all 200). BOTH or no shot
dev_gate.the_base_is_measured_here: the base's dev numbers are MEASURED in this session on the same pod, never assumed and never taken from another run. That is what «paired» means
dev_gate.when: rung 7, before the shot, on the Mac

judge.absent_or_refusal: a DISAGREEMENT — silence about a row that was asked is a miss
judge.rule: the same bytes probe-b and lora-b were scored with. A new equality loop would be a second definition of the bar and is refused

scorer_pass1_fewshot.rule: D2's judge, pinned. r1 named the bar and left the file that computes it unpinned (Dv606) — the same class as lora-b's Dv584, one contract later. It is the same script r1 committed at c7cbfd1 with its two record paths moved to r2's

kill_clock.read: costPerHr in the create response is the meter of record (Dv448)
kill_clock.rule: live price > $0.8/h at create → STOP, no endpoint. The backstop stamp is checked against the cumulative hard stop in the same command

kill_clock.read: money.arithmetic.ssh_rule — the spread this ceiling is, and the two readings
kill_clock.rule: ssh dead-man ≤ 500 s of this pod's create-elapsed or KILL. r1's 180 s was pass1-probe's reading of one night: it passed on 2026-08-18 and failed on BOTH pods of 2026-08-20, on the same card in the same datacenter (Dv602). The new ceiling is a spread, and one dead pod under it costs $0.1111

kill_clock.backstop_rule: and a create-anchored BACKSTOP beside it: first reply ≤ 1100 s of create-elapsed or KILL — ssh 500 + stage/launch 150 + load 450. It is what bounds the launch anchor: a stamp taken late cannot buy a window the registration never priced, and the backstop fires with no human in the path
kill_clock.read: the `launched_at` stamp the runbook writes into the pod's run directory the moment the runner starts, copied back by --watch and recorded in results/pass1_fewshot_r2_run.json
kill_clock.rule: launch → first reply ≤ 450 s of the runner's OWN `launched_at` or KILL. r1 derived this ceiling from the model-LOAD window and measured it from create, and the two spans are not the same one: create-elapsed also carries the ssh wait, the staging and the launch, and the two spans this stack has MEASURED already exceed it together (Dv605). A run record without `launched_at` cannot report GO on this rung — a deadline that cannot be demonstrated has not been passed

kill_clock.before: the run is allowed to continue past a call
kill_clock.rule: projection gate every 20 calls: the projected attempt total at MEASURED rates, with every leg still owed priced, must fit the cap at the LIVE price AND the cumulative hard stop, else KILL

kill_clock.read: held by scripts/gate_pass1_fewshot.py --watch, a BLOCKING loop
kill_clock.rule: liveness: 600 s with no new answered row and no new pod-log line → KILL. The deadline is measured from the LAST EVENT and never from create. The executor does not poll by hand and does not leave the loop — lora-b lost 9 720 s and an arm because every rung there watched the training log and none watched a pod that had stopped working

kill_clock.read: the `--terminate-after` stamp, read back and refused on overshoot
kill_clock.rule: cumulative hard stop 6100 s, PLATFORM-held. Each pod's --terminate-after is its own create plus what the stop has left, and the overshoot it forgives is the registered 60 s

kill_clock.read: bars.dev_gate — both inequalities, paired on the same 200 rows
kill_clock.rule: dev gate: our_v2 − our_base ≥ 10 AND agree_v2 − agree_base ≥ -5. Both or NO shot. RED → delete, prove it by listing, the attempt is NOT spent, and the table returns to the team lead
the shot is 64 units into its OWN out-file, never a dev leg's — the shipped resume skips every id it already sees (Dv560). The attempt is SPENT at the first gold-row reply

arithmetic.boot_rule: UNCHANGED from r1 — ≥ the worst boot this stack has measured (353.0 s, lora-b) by ×1.2748. What r2 moves is not the ceiling but the SPAN it is measured over: r1 derived it from the model-load window and applied it to create-elapsed, which also carries the ssh wait, the staging and the launch (Dv605). In r2 it is anchored on the runner's own `launched_at`

cumulative.backstop_tolerance_rule: how far the `--terminate-after` stamp actually handed to `pod create` may sit BEYOND the one the hard stop computes. Only overshoot is bounded — a window rounded DOWN shortens itself and is always safe. It lived in the gate's source in r1 (Dv603) and the gate now READS it from here; a record without this field is a refusal, not a default
cumulative.hard_stop_rule: cumulative billed ≤ 6100 s = $1.3556 at the $0.8/h ceiling. It sits UNDER the $1.38 cap it defends, and it is the PLATFORM that enforces it — so it protects even a hung call no gate can see

projection_gate.formula: billed_by_closed_pods + elapsed_on_this_pod + Σ over every leg still owed of (its remaining calls × its s/call) + overhead_seconds. A leg with a reply is priced at its MEASURED rate — the larger of its mean and its last call; a leg with none is priced at the LARGER of its registered rate and the worst rate measured on this pod so far
projection_gate.overhead_rule: the SAME 1300 s the money block charges, and it has to be: rung 4 prices the attempt with it on every poll, so a second copy here is a second budget. H6 asserts the two are one number
projection_gate.verdict: KILL if the projection exceeds $1.38 at the LIVE price, or exceeds the 6100 s hard stop in seconds. The stricter binds
projection_gate.why_every_leg: the shot's 64 calls are what makes the dev legs affordable at all. A projection that priced only the running leg would open a run the cap closes

cumulative.rule: the hard stop and EVERY budget check count across ALL pods of this attempt, never per pod. `--terminate-after` on each pod is stamped at that pod's create plus the hard stop LESS what every closed pod already billed, so two pods cannot each be given a fresh window
cumulative.session_ceiling_rule: cap / price ceiling — the longest session the cap can pay for. It is ≥ the hard stop, so the platform-held stop is the binding one and the cap is never what discovers an overrun

arithmetic.overhead_rule: 1300 s (r1: 1800) — the scp of 464 answered rows and the pod log, the dev gate on the Mac, and the deletion with its three listings. It is SMALLER than r1's because the ssh wait and the staging now have their own lines: the reduction of 500 s is covered by the 650 s those lines add, so nothing is counted twice and nothing is dropped
arithmetic.pre_generation_rule: ssh 500 + stage/launch 150 + load 450 = 1100 s, and it is ALSO rung 3's create-anchored backstop. The three spans are priced separately because r1 priced them as one and the one was named for the shortest of them

recovery_arithmetic.a_second_dead_pod: STOP. After a second dead pod nothing fits and the session closes with the attempt NOT spent — a THIRD pod under this registration is refused by the arithmetic and by this record. `--pre-create-check` READS `re_creations_allowed` and refuses the create itself, because at two CHEAP deaths the seconds would still fit and only the count says no
recovery_arithmetic.rule: the recovery clause must stay REACHABLE after one dead pod, and that is what fixes rung 2 at 500 s. One dead pod plus the full worst case is 5976.552 s ≤ 6100 and $1.3281 ≤ $1.38, so ONE re-creation fits by the registered arithmetic. `--pre-create-check` computes both bounds before every create and the stricter binds
recovery_arithmetic.why_not_600: a 600 s rung 2 grows the worst case itself to 5576.552 s, so one dead pod plus that worst case is 6176.552 s — PAST the 6100 s hard stop. The dollars would still fit; the seconds do not, and the seconds are what the platform holds

seconds_per_call.rule: base is MEASURED — probe-b's 64 paid calls on an RTX 4090, mean 5.162 s. v2 is UNMEASURED and is registered as a BOUND: 1.5 × the measured base, for the longer prefill five labelled examples add. Rung 4 measures it at call 20 and every 20 after that, and the projection then prices the rest at what the pod is actually doing
seconds_per_call.sample: results/pass1_probe_b_rows.jsonl — 64 calls, one card, one boot. Named beside the number because a rate is a property of the sample it was measured on

arithmetic.ssh_rule: rung 2's own ceiling, charged as a line of the budget. It is a SPREAD and not a measurement: probe-b saw ssh at 14.5 s on this card in this datacenter on 2026-08-18, and on 2026-08-20 two pods were still `pod not ready` at 262.5 s and 231.9 s — both of them LOWER bounds, because ssh was never observed up. The ceiling is ×2.1561 the smaller of the two
arithmetic.stage_launch_rule: scp of the bundle and the runners, the clone, the volume check and the detached launch. probe-b bounds all of it at ≤ 89.5 s (657 s billed − 237.155 s of load − 330.3 s of generation) INCLUDING its own ssh wait, so ×1.676 of a bound that is already generous is what this line buys

money.cap_rule: $1.38 all-in for r2, frozen at the FIRST `pod create`. It is not a new budget: the STEP's budget is $1.50 and r1's pods already bought $0.117783 of it. Raising it is the operator's word BEFORE any endpoint exists, never after a reading
money.guard: PYTHONPATH=src python3.11 scripts/runpod_guard.py --step pass1-fewshot-r2 --step-cap 1.38 — the anchor is committed BEFORE the pod exists, and the reading is what the rungs that name one act on. r1's step ledger is closed and is never re-anchored

meter.datacenter: EU-RO-1, pinned by network volume qw4nwleanc — the volume decides
meter.memory: this line does NOT train, so lora-b's 48 GB constraint does not apply: probe-b served this same base on a 24 GB 4090. That makes rung 1 a price gate against a much wider market than lora-b faced
meter.price_rule: **READ ON THE DAY.** `costPerHr` in the create response is the meter of record and every figure here is recomputed from it by rung 4 before the run is allowed to continue
meter.resource: ONE rented pod, billed for every second it EXISTS — from `pod create` to `pod delete`. `pod stop` does not stop the bill, so the run deletes and never stops

reading.rule: money is read from the GUARD, never from a ledger and never from prose (Dv33)

arithmetic.a_second_dead_pod: STOP. After a second dead pod nothing fits and the session closes with the attempt NOT spent — a THIRD pod under this registration is refused by the arithmetic and by this record. `--pre-create-check` READS `re_creations_allowed` and refuses the create itself, because at two CHEAP deaths the seconds would still fit and only the count says no
arithmetic.rule: the recovery clause must stay REACHABLE after one dead pod, and that is what fixes rung 2 at 500 s. arithmetic.why_not_600: a 600 s rung 2 grows the worst case itself to 5576.552 s, so one dead pod plus that worst case is 6176.552 s — PAST the 6100 s hard stop. The dollars would still fit; the seconds do not, and the seconds are what the platform holds

recovery.rule: ONE pod re-creation, and only after a deletion PROVEN by listing. It happens only if the guard READING plus the worst case remaining at MEASURED rates is ≤ $1.38 and inside the cumulative stop. recovery.there_is_no_generation_checkpoint_to_los: every reply is flushed to its out-file as it lands and the shipped resume skips every unit already answered, so a re-creation re-asks only what has no reply. That is the one thing this line has that lora-b did not: a KILL mid-leg costs the boot, not the leg
